purpose: Define a behavioral partner-force capability outcome independently of the indigenous autonomy predictors.
baseline: At withdrawal time T, both ON and OFF branches receive the exact same CapabilityAssayBaseline containing military fielded personnel, operational formation count, geographic coverage, and personnel-weighted deployable operational readiness. A separate baseline at T-60 is used only to measure pre-withdrawal supported performance.

components.territorial_control: mean government effective control across localities, bounded [0,1]
components.personnel_retention: fielded operational military personnel / shared T baseline personnel, clipped [0,1]
components.formation_survival: operational military formation count / shared T baseline formation count, clipped [0,1]
components.coverage_retention: distinct localities covered by operational military formations / shared T baseline coverage, clipped [0,1]
components.operational_readiness_retention: personnel-weighted deployable operational readiness / shared T baseline readiness, clipped [0,1]

predictor_firewall: training/recruitment throughput is not a component of C
logistics production/delivery is not a component of C
command reliability/latency is not a component of C
external support quantities and donor cost are not components of C
formal autonomy metrics (q-, q+, support lift, bottleneck) are candidate predictors, not components of C
interpretation: C is a synthetic behavioral assay for Pineland incorporating territorial control, force retention, formation survival, geographic presence, and deployable operational readiness, not a validated real-world military-effectiveness index.
